- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects; apply lagged mean reversion to dampen immediate rise.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3–5 day moving average as baseline.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model tends to ignore volatility; add 1–2% downward bias for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or negative, model often overestimates; apply 3–5% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is below 60.00.
